answer: An agent’s identity is bound to an enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) verified in a hardware-signed remote attestation, so copying a VM image alone cannot reproduce the trusted proof. Creating additional accepted identities therefore requires access to genuine attested silicon, raising the cost of Sybil attacks rather than making them impossible. The grove of identities can grow only as trusted hardware capacity expands, limiting the ripple of cheap virtual duplication across the bridge to consensus.
